subject: Post-demo: BrightAI budget bands, token econ & procurement path
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@brightai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 May 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: BrightAI budget bands, token econ & procurement path

Hey Liam / Emma —

Thanks again for making time for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a proposed set of next steps so we can validate budget / procurement gating on your side. I captured the pricing/volume assumptions we discussed and a recommended commitment band to avoid surprises when you scale.

Key points from the call
- Workload profile: user-facing summarization + two internal reranking jobs. Expected median prompt length ~120 tokens, median generation ~80 tokens.
- Current pilot target: ~1–2M generated tokens per day (peak spikes to ~3.5M/day during marketing campaigns).
- Redwood unit economics we discussed: list price baseline $35 / 1M tokens for the gen model; recommended committed band gives blended $25–$28 / 1M depending on commit and burst policies.
- Procurement note: PO threshold for your legal/procurement was discussed as $75k per purchase order to avoid longer approval cycles.

My proposal (conservative, to align with your procurement windows)
1) Pilot commit: 30 days, 30M total generated tokens (roughly $900–840 at $30–$28 /1M) — effectively a small paid pilot that buys down unit price and simplifies procurement.
2) If pilot hits 50%+ of expected volume within 2 weeks, convert to a 3-month committed band: 90–120M / month (blended pricing target $25 / 1M).
3) PO/contract route: If you need a single PO >$75k, we recommend a quarterly invoice schedule (Redwood accepts quarterly invoices for Dedicated/pilot commits).

Attachments: I attached a short pricing worksheet (redwood-pricing-illustration.xlsx) that shows the blended math at different commit levels and a summarized copy of the demo notes.

Next steps I suggest
- You confirm whether the $75k PO threshold is the right procurement gate (or if $50k is acceptable).
- Your finance/procurement contact to loop in (if different from Emma).
- If you want, I can draft a small mutual action plan (MAP) with dates and criteria for conversion.

Happy to hop on a 20-minute follow-up tomorrow if that helps — otherwise please reply with the procurement threshold and any questions on the worksheet.

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

--
Attachment: redwood-pricing-illustration.xlsx (spreadsheet, 24KB)
Attachment: brightai-demo-notes.pdf (pdf, 58KB)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@brightai.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Park <emma.park@brightai.com>
Date: Wed, 10 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: BrightAI budget bands, token econ & procurement path

Jonas —

Appreciate the clear recap and the worksheet. A few clarifications from our side:
- The volume numbers look right as a high-level estimate. Our product analytics team expects the steady-state to be closer to 40–50M gen tokens / month if we open the feature to all customers right away (spike tolerance is a bit higher than we discussed).
- Procurement: our current PO threshold before exec sign-off is $60k. We do occasionally bundle monthly invoices into a single quarter PO to hit higher thresholds.
- Finance asks: can you show a sample invoice schedule for the pilot that keeps each invoice under $60k? That will help us avoid extra approvals.

Also, Emma will be the finance/procurement owner here — copying her. If she needs more detail I can connect you both to our procurement portal.

Liam
Head of Product | BrightAI
liam.oconnor@brightai.com

Date: Fri, 12 May 2028 11:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: BrightAI budget bands, token econ & procurement path

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the note and for looping Emma in. Quick operational answers from our side that should help frame what procurement will need: 

1) Invoice cadence: We can split the pilot into two invoices (front-loaded + final) so each invoice stays under $60k. Example: for a $90k pilot we can do $45k at start / $45k at completion (net 30 each).
2) Discounts & PO: We can provide the committed-band blended price tier in the pilot MSA and the pricing worksheet—no need for an extra contract amendment in most cases. If BrightAI prefers a single quarter PO >$60k, we can do quarterly invoicing too; we just need the PO number and billing contact.
3) Billing contacts & required fields: procurement likes a dedicated billing email and a PO reference line. If Emma can confirm billing contact and whether they require an SOW attachment, we’ll include that.

I’ll draft a 1-page MAP (internal milestone + success criteria + billing milestones) and share it early next week. Jonas — can you add the two splitting invoice line items (numbers) into the worksheet and share an updated copy?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Thanks — that approach works for us.

Confirmed next steps from BrightAI:
- Emma will issue a pilot PO for $54,000 (two invoices of $27,000 each) to keep under our $60k approval gate. PO target delivery date: 2028-05-20.
- We'll run the 30-day pilot you proposed (30M tokens) and share weekly usage snapshots; if we hit ~50%+ of expected throughput we'll move toward the 3-month committed band conversation.
- Procurement will upload the PO to your billing portal; Emma will reply with the PO number once it's posted.

I'll mark Jonas/Marissa as our points of contact for billing & success.

Liam
